newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, supply looms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, supply looms.

text.p: U.S. muni cash prices opened unchanged but firm as players eyed this week's primary market where roughly $3.9 billion of fresh debt is expected.
"It's firm, obviously, (with) follow through from Friday," one trader said, adding that action was light. "I think the market is going to be dominated this week by the primary calendar."
The calendar contains "a good mix of inventory," he said. A second trader also judged the market even but firm, with the focus on the new issues.
"There's a lot of deals coming here this week," he said.
Competitive deals are expected to total $1.7 billion in 105 issues, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. Negotiated sales are expected to number 48 and total $2.2 billion.

The biggest competitive deal is a $320 million Los Angeles Harbor Department, Calif., deal slated for Wednesday. The largest negotiated deal expected is a $281 million New York State Dormitory via Goldman Sachs & Co.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury was down 8/32 at 101-20/32 to yield 6.38 percent. The decline follows Friday's sharp rally.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was down 6/32 at 117-24/32. The March T-bond contract was down 6/32 at 115-22/32. The MOB spread was 66 ticks.

On the data front, the U.S. Commerce Department is expected to issue October construction spending at 1000 EST. Economists in a Reuters Survey expect a decline of 1.0 percent compared with a 1.9 percent increase from the previous report.
Also at 1000 (EST), the National Association of Purchasing Management is expected to issue its November survey of business activity in the manufacturing sector.
